newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Aussie Gold - Gold seen steady after rough ride.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Aussie Gold - Gold seen steady after rough ride.

text.p: Gold is expected to stabilise near current price levels over the mid-term as the market resumes more normal trading patterns after a tumultuous month, Australian bullion dealers said on Wednesday.
Gold was fetching about A$452 an ounce early on Wednesday, not a great price for Australian gold companies, but one they can live with given forward hedging, the dealers said.
"Most (miners) are resolved to a gold price at around this price," one said.

Due to forward positions that Western Australia miner Great Central Mines Ltd has in place, it should be able to realise a gold price of A$540-A$550 an ounce over the next 18 months, even if the spot Australian dollar gold price remains at A$450 an ounce, broker Bell Securities Ltd said.

Normandy Mining Ltd, which among other properties owns a 50 percent stake in the big Super Pit gold mine in Western Australia, has 5.86 million ounces sold forward at an average price of A$722 an ounce.
Newcrest Mining Ltd has said some 3.7 million ounces are hedged in forward sales and options positions at an average of US$490 an ounce over nine years.
The Perth Mint, Australia's largest gold refiner, on Wednesday quoted a spot gold selling price of A$457.24 an ounce (US$354.64 an ounce).
Gold was fixed at $353.10 on Tuesday afternoon in London.
Prices have climbed strongly over the past two weeks after hitting a 3-3/4 year low around $336 on February 12.
Dealers said they expected few fireworks when February over-the-counter options expire later on Wednesday, with the market focusing on the strike prices of US$350 and US$355 an ounce.
Fundamentally, dealers said gold was showing gains, noting particular interest among some Asian fabricating setors as well as the Middle Eastern jewellery sector.
